clue.text: Memorable passing comment?

parts.note: passing is read as dying, so the memorable comment is the one somebody makes just before death

explanation.surface: Someone recalls a striking remark made in passing during a conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Passing' looks like 'casual, in passing', but here it means dying. The phrase is also used ironically for a confident prediction that soon proves wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: The final utterance of a dying person, often quoted afterwards, is a memorable remark made at death.

clue.text: Canonised dame who acts for the team

parts.note: a canonised person is a saint, abbreviated ST
Dame Helen Mirren is a celebrated British actress

explanation.surface: A sainted dame performs on behalf of her side.
explanation.walkthrough: ST MIRREN is a Scottish football club from Paisley.
explanation.definitionFit: A Scottish professional football club is a sporting side.

clue.text: Weep about relegation, initially — something to say for promotion?

indicators.note: about means the word for weeping goes around the other piece

parts.note: to blub is to cry, an informal word for weeping

indicators.note: initially means only the first letter of relegation is used

explanation.surface: A football fan cries over relegation, wondering what could be said in favour of going up.
explanation.walkthrough: Promotion is advertising here, not a club moving up a division, which the football picture of relegation suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A publisher's short promotional description on a book jacket is written to sell it.

clue.text: Spooner's gin more damaging for baby-minder?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so these two words have their starts exchanged

parts.note: a gin is a trap, as is a net
more damaging means worse

explanation.surface: A drinker wonders whether gin would be more harmful to a babysitter.
explanation.walkthrough: Gin is the snare, not the drink. Swapping the opening sounds of NET WORSE gives the answer by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman employed to breastfeed and care for another's infant is a minder of babies.

clue.text: Some high-water mark?

parts.note: the punctuation mark joining high and water in the clue's own compound word is the mark meant

explanation.surface: A query about a tidal level marked on a harbour wall.
explanation.walkthrough: A high-water mark is the line a flood or tide reaches; read literally, 'high-water' itself carries a mark, the dash between its parts.
explanation.definitionFit: The short dash linking the halves of a compound word is a punctuation mark.

clue.text: A Roman emperor seizing power in a month, becoming president in South America

indicators.note: in means the whole of this sits within the month

parts.note: JUN is the short form of June

indicators.note: seizing means the emperor's name holds the letter for power inside it

parts.note: Nero was a Roman emperor

explanation.surface: An ancient emperor grabs power within a month and turns into a Latin American head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A Roman emperor seizing power' gives A NPERO; that sits in JUN.
explanation.definitionFit: Juan Perón was the populist leader who held the presidency of Argentina.

clue.text: Scalpel shaving odd parts in the middle of genuine central bits

indicators.note: in means the even letters go inside the other piece
the middle of picks out the central three letters of genuine
shaving off the odd-numbered letters of scalpel leaves its even ones

explanation.surface: A surgeon's blade trims away odd pieces from the core of something real.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shaving odd parts' keeps the second, fourth and sixth letters; 'the middle of' takes the central three letters of a seven-letter word, not just one.
explanation.definitionFit: Cores or central parts around which other things gather are the plural of nucleus.

clue.text: Band consumes starter of seven fresh sardines after American condiment

indicators.note: consumes means the band swallows the rest inside it

parts.note: a ring is a band

indicators.note: after means the following pieces come behind the American abbreviation
starter of means the first letter of seven
fresh means the letters of sardines are made anew in another order

explanation.surface: A band of musicians eats some newly caught fish following an American.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fresh' gives IANDRESS from the fish; 'Band' is a ring, not a group of musicians, and 'consumes' wraps it around everything else.
explanation.definitionFit: A creamy salad sauce made with mayonnaise and ketchup or chilli is a condiment.

clue.text: Arms requiring medication where blood flows?

indicators.note: where puts the sick piece in the place named next, inside it

parts.note: an artery is a vessel through which blood flows
someone who needs medicine is ill

explanation.surface: Someone's arms need treatment at the point where blood runs.
explanation.walkthrough: Arms are weapons, not limbs, despite the medical picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Large guns and heavy weaponry are military arms.

clue.text: Australian place of worship full, church capturing all hearts

indicators.note: all hearts means the central letters of each of the next three words are taken

explanation.surface: An Australian church is packed, drawing in everyone emotionally.
explanation.walkthrough: The hearts are UL, UR and U, the middles of full, church and capturing.
explanation.definitionFit: The great red rock in central Australia is a sacred site for its Aboriginal owners.

clue.text: Greek character working over Spanish artist, about a hundred

indicators.note: over means the word for working covers the rest, around it

parts.note: a machine that is on is working

indicators.note: about means the artist goes around the hundred

parts.note: Joan Miró was a Spanish painter
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred

explanation.surface: A Greek person is at work on a painting by a Spaniard, priced around a hundred.
explanation.definitionFit: The fifteenth letter of the Greek alphabet is a character in that script.

clue.text: See 22
Fine to admit to deviant urges? Yes!

indicators.note: to admit to means the word for fine is let inside the other piece
deviant means the letters of urges stray from their order

parts.note: fine means thin, as in a fine thread

explanation.surface: Someone asks if it is all right to confess to perverse desires, and gets an emphatic answer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deviant' gives SUREG; 'Fine' means slender here, not acceptable, as the question-and-answer surface suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: A certainty, said as an emphatic agreement, works as an enthusiastic affirmative reply.

clue.text: Supporter welcoming spirit in a couple of players

indicators.note: welcoming means the supporter takes the other pieces inside

parts.note: a bra is a supporting undergarment
an angel is a spirit
in is taken as written

explanation.surface: A supporter brings a spirit into a pair of performers.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is the media's blended name for actors Brad Pitt and Angelina Jolie.
explanation.definitionFit: Two film actors who were a celebrity couple are a pair of performers.

clue.text: The red pea soup is prepared for cooking

indicators.note: soup suggests ingredients mixed together, so these letters are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: A red pea soup gets ready for the stove.
explanation.definitionFit: An oven warmed up in advance is readied for cooking.

clue.text: Racecourse fair, cryptically?

parts.note: the word fair is the letter A placed inside fir, a tree

explanation.surface: A racecourse is described as fair, with a hint to read it slyly.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as wordplay, A in tree: put A inside FIR, a tree, and you get FAIR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Merseyside track that stages the Grand National steeplechase is a racecourse.

clue.text: Continue supporting top tennis player, vocally

indicators.note: vocally means the words are spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: pro means supporting and a seed is a top-ranked tennis player

explanation.surface: Someone keeps backing a leading tennis star, out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To go on or carry on is to continue.

clue.text: Horse entering river has left a path following an arc

indicators.note: entering means the horse goes inside the river

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river
an Arab is a breed of horse

explanation.surface: A horse wades into a river and has left a trail that curves.
explanation.definitionFit: A curve like the flight of a thrown ball is the path traced by a projectile.

clue.text: Wickedness a precious thing amid bad blood

indicators.note: amid means the gold sits in the middle of the other piece

parts.note: bad blood between people is enmity
or is the heraldic word for gold, a precious metal

explanation.surface: Something precious caught up in a feud breeds wickedness.
explanation.definitionFit: Great evil or outrageousness of an act is its heinousness, its moral monstrousness.

clue.text: To peep effin' dangerous, seeing visitor to bedroom in secret

parts.note: to peep, like a car horn, is to toot
effin' splits as F IN, so the letter F goes inside hairy, slang for dangerous

explanation.surface: Swearing at a risky peeping Tom who sneaks into bedrooms.
explanation.walkthrough: The mild oath 'effin'' is really F IN: the letter F placed inside HAIRY, British slang for scary or risky.
explanation.definitionFit: The children's figure who swaps a coin for a lost milk tooth calls at night unseen.

clue.text: I see no problem getting comprehensive cover

indicators.note: problem signals the letters are in trouble and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone shrugs off any difficulty in arranging full insurance.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-piece garment covering the whole body is all-over clothing.

clue.text: Raising money in Sweden, inspiring a geek

indicators.note: inspiring means breathing the letter A in, so it goes inside
raising in a down entry means the currency is written upwards, backwards

parts.note: the krona is Sweden's currency

explanation.surface: A fundraiser in Sweden motivates a nerd.
explanation.walkthrough: Turned upwards, KRONA gives ANORK, which takes A inside.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang a socially awkward obsessive enthusiast is called by the name of a hooded jacket.

clue.text: Nothing takes care of a bulging waistline

parts.note: love means nothing, a zero score in tennis
to deal with something is to manage it

explanation.surface: Nothing deals with a spreading middle.
explanation.definitionFit: Rolls of fat at the sides of the waist are an informal term for a thickening middle.

clue.text: See 13
22 12 on a daughter of the Bard added flavour

parts.note: the paired cross-reference reads as zero handles, two round letters attached either side like handles on a pot
Regan is one of King Lear's daughters in Shakespeare's play
the paired cross-reference reads as zero handles, two round letters attached either side like handles on a pot

explanation.surface: Cross-referenced entries put on a Shakespearean daughter gave extra taste.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference means love handles: love is O, and the two O's sit either side of REGAN like handles. The Bard is Shakespeare.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mediterranean herb is used in cooking to season food.

clue.text: Island nation awarding degree to Islamic organisation

parts.note: BA is a Bachelor of Arts degree
Hamas is a Palestinian Islamist organisation

explanation.surface: An island country grants an academic qualification to a religious group.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean archipelago state is a country made of islands.

clue.text: Cricket shot sees opener in Rawalpindi breaking duck

indicators.note: breaking means the letter breaks into the other word

parts.note: to duck under water is to dive

indicators.note: opener in means the first letter of Rawalpindi

explanation.surface: A batsman in Pakistan plays a shot that ends his run of no scores.
explanation.walkthrough: Duck is a cricket score of nought, but here it means plunge.
explanation.definitionFit: A forceful straight batting stroke along the ground is a standard cricket stroke.

clue.text: Northern English town wanting the first location for a national cemetery

indicators.note: wanting the first means lacking the opening letter

parts.note: Darlington is a town in County Durham, north-east England

explanation.surface: A northern town lacks the original site for a war graveyard.
explanation.definitionFit: The Virginia site across the Potomac from Washington holds America's best-known military graveyard.
